name: PocketFFT (C++ branch)
workload: 3D real-to-complex FFT, 256x256x256 single precision, plus 1D/2D complex FFTs, in a third-party shootout
claimed_speedup: 3D R2C 256^3: PocketFFT AVX 97 ms vs KissFFT 436 ms (4.5x, derived from page data); 416x256x416: 311 ms vs 2078 ms; 3D C2C 256^3: 264 ms vs 785 ms; also 'as fast as FFTW3' for AVX R2C (97 ms vs fftw3 meas. 98 ms)
hardware: Intel i7-5600U, 4 threads @ 3200 MHz, L1 32K L2 256K L3 4096K
stars_or_usage: 148 stars; used inside NumPy and SciPy (per benchmark README)
tradeoffs: Vectorized only for multi-D or batched transforms via GCC/Clang vector_size; 1D not SIMD, so 1D C2C 512 (4009 ns) is far slower than FFTW with SIMD (588 ns). Very fast plan generation (1274 ns vs 25610 ns FFTW).
caveats: Benchmark is by a user (gemmi author) of the library; FFTW binaries from Ubuntu 18.04 not self-built; MKL 2019 is faster (61 ms R2C 256^3). Old CPU/compiler. KissFFT rows are non-SIMD builds. Repo README itself gives no numbers. Last commit date not confirmed.
found_via: WebSearch: C++ FFT library faster than FFTW benchmark github -> project-gemmi/benchmarking-fft

name: muFFT
workload: 1D complex FFT n=512 and 2D complex FFT 256x256, single precision, in the gemmi shootout
claimed_speedup: 1D C2C n=512: muFFT 719 ns (SIMD) / 4024 ns (no SIMD) vs KissFFT 6553 ns; 2D 256x256 muFFT NS 1092 us vs kissfft NS 1583 us. Versus FFTW3 (meas.) muFFT is competitive: 259 us vs 306 us (2D 256x256), 719 vs 588 ns (1D 512, slower)
hardware: Intel i7-5600U, 4 threads @ 3200 MHz, L1 32K L2 256K L3 4096K
tradeoffs: Power-of-two only (n/a for 384/480); radix 4/8 only; SSE/SSE3/AVX paths, NEON planned; muFFT-bench/test binaries are GPL-2.0+ because of FFTW linkage.
caveats: 1D KissFFT figure (6553 ns) is the non-SIMD run; the SIMD muFFT vs scalar KissFFT comparison inflates the ratio. Repo README has no numbers (only 'usually competitive' with FFTW3 and FFmpeg). Does not beat FFTW in 1D 512.
found_via: WebSearch: header-only SIMD FFT library benchmark vs FFTW MKL KissFFT pocketfft -> gemmi shootout

name: PFFFT (marton78 fork)
workload: 1D complex FFT n=256..512 and real FFT, single precision, in the gemmi shootout
claimed_speedup: 1D C2C n=512: pffft 1255 ns (SIMD) vs KissFFT 6553 ns (derived 5.2x); pffft NS 3792 ns vs 6553 ns; R2C n=512: pffft 597 ns vs kissfft NS 2985 ns. Roughly on par with FFTW est.: 585 ns vs 321 ns at n=256 (slower than FFTW)
hardware: Intel i7-5600U, 4 threads @ 3200 MHz, L1 32K L2 256K L3 4096K
tradeoffs: Size must be a multiple of 16 (complex) or 32 (real) with SIMD; single precision (fork adds double); README says goal is >=50% of fastest FFT, not records. Output ordering differs.
caveats: Compared against KissFFT scalar; slower than FFTW and MKL. Marked license text 'BSD-like' not a verified SPDX id. Original is Julien Pommier's bitbucket pffft (fork additions). Separate benchmark repo hayguen/pffft_benchmarks has per-CPU results I could not read in detail.
found_via: WebSearch: C++ FFT library faster than FFTW benchmark github -> marton78/pffft

name: meow_fft
workload: Complex FFT N=1024 and N=8192 vs kiss_fft and pffft
claimed_speedup: N=1024: 8.89 us vs kiss_fft 13.12 us; N=8192: 84.72 us vs 119.38 us (derived ~1.4-1.5x). Gemmi shootout: n=512 C2C no-SIMD 4342 ns vs KissFFT 6553 ns
tradeoffs: C99 single header, no explicit SIMD, radix-8 kernel; slower than pffft, muFFT, vDSP and FFTW by author's own statement; no 2D/3D.
caveats: Author's README table is first-party; a second independent set (gemmi) agrees on direction. Tier B per independent shootout but without gemmi's own meow row for all sizes. Gemmi readme listed 2017 start. Does not beat FFTW.
found_via: WebSearch: C++ FFT library faster than FFTW benchmark github -> gemmi shootout, then meow_fft README

name: KFR
workload: FFT of power-of-2, prime, composite and random sizes against FFTW, Intel MKL, Intel IPP (graphs in README; harness in kfrlib/fft-benchmark)
claimed_speedup: Graphs only: KFR shown faster than FFTW on power-of-2 sizes 16..16,777,216 (no numeric values on page)
compiler_and_flags: Clang recommended (16+); fft-benchmark README lists C++17, Clang 12+ recommended; no flags stated
tradeoffs: Dual license: GPL or paid commercial; best performance needs Clang; SSE2-AVX512, NEON, RVV; broader DSP framework.
caveats: First-party graphs, no numbers or CPU on pages I opened; the gemmi author did not benchmark KFR. The fft-benchmark repo (MIT, 14 libs incl. FFTW/MKL/KissFFT/PocketFFT/PFFFT) is reproducible but its README has no results, no CPU/compiler. Does not list a dependable license SPDX beyond README text.
found_via: WebSearch: C++ FFT library faster than FFTW benchmark github -> kfrlib/kfr and kfrlib/fft-benchmark

name: VkFFT
workload: Batched 1D FFTs of lengths 2..4096 (500MB-1GB total), double precision, bandwidth estimate, vs cuFFT (CUDA 11.7) and rocFFT (ROCm 5.2)
claimed_speedup: README states it aims for 'better performance' than cuFFT; results are plots (benchmark_plot/fp64_cuda_a100.png, fp64_hip_mi250.png), no numbers on page
hardware: Nvidia A100 and AMD MI250 GPUs
tradeoffs: GPU library (Vulkan/CUDA/HIP/OpenCL/Level Zero/Metal), runtime kernel generation; header-only C API. Not a CPU FFTW alternative.
caveats: Baseline cuFFT is not in the category list (GPU incumbent). Numbers only in images I did not read. OpenBenchmarking page runs VkFFT only, no cuFFT comparison. Precision claim: more precise than cuFFT/rocFFT with FP128 twiddles.

name: ducc (ducc0.fft)
workload: Multi-dimensional FFTs in single precision (README design notes)
claimed_speedup: README: multi-D double precision 'fairly similar' to FFTW_MEASURE; single precision 'can be significantly faster'; no numbers. Concedes 1D is somewhat slower than FFTW
license: GPL-2.0 (BSD for FFT components per repo page)
tradeoffs: C++17, multithreading, NUFFT, SHT; Python bindings; 1D slower than FFTW.
caveats: No numbers in README; a performance page at mtr.pages.mpcdf.de/ducc was referenced but not opened. License mix not verified file by file. Last commit date not seen.
